points.title: Data flow diagram
points.must: Definition: shows how data moves through a system — inputs, processes, data stores and outputs; shows what happens to data, not how or in what order.

points.title: Why and when DFDs are used
points.must: Common language for client, analyst and programmers; drawn at analysis (current system) and design (new system); stores → database tables, processes → program parts, entity flows → input screens / outputs.

points.title: Logical, not physical
points.must: A DFD shows what data moves, not hardware, software, people, time, order or decisions; no 'computer' or 'printer' boxes.

points.title: External entity
points.must: Person / organisation / system outside the system that sends data in (source) or receives data out (sink); rectangle; named with a noun; example.

points.title: Process
points.must: Action inside the system that transforms input data into output data; rounded rectangle with a number; verb + noun name; example.

points.title: Data store
points.must: Data held for later use (file, table); open-ended rectangle with ID D1, D2…; noun name; example.

points.title: Data flow
points.must: Data moving between symbols; arrow showing direction; labelled with the name of the data (noun), never an action.

points.title: Drawing of the four symbols
points.must: A labelled sketch of all four Gane–Sarson symbols (or a consistent alternative notation).

points.title: Input and output in a DFD
points.must: Input = flow from an entity to a process (becomes an input form); output = flow from a process to an entity (receipt, report); a flow into a store is NOT an output; examples.

points.title: Processing and storage in a DFD
points.must: Processing = processes, output data differs from input; storage = data stores, process→store = write, store→process = read; each store written and read; scenario keywords (kept, saved, recorded).

points.title: Reading a DFD as IPOS (worked example)
points.must: Canteen or clinic example: inputs, processes, stores (reads/writes) and outputs listed, and a missing part spotted.

points.title: Context diagram and system boundary
points.must: Level 0: whole system as ONE process with all external entities and flows; no data stores; boundary = inside (processes, stores) vs outside (entities); how to decide (e.g. bank is outside).

points.title: Level-1 DFD and levels
points.must: Decomposes the single process into main processes (3–7) numbered 1, 2, 3; adds data stores; table of context / level 1 / level 2.

points.title: Balancing
points.must: Level-1 DFD has the same external entities and the same flows in and out as the context diagram; new flows only inside the boundary; library or canteen example.

points.title: Common mistakes
points.must: Stores on a context diagram; noun-only process names; action words on flows; computer/database as an entity; flow into a store called an output; vague flow names.
